newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria grants licence to 48 telecoms firms.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria grants licence to 48 telecoms firms.

text.p: LAGOS, June 2 (REUTER) - Nigeria has given approval to a new set of 48 private companies to provide a variety of telecommunications services, newspapers reported on Monday.

They said the National Communications Commission (NCC) granted the licences to cover a range of services including the provision of mobile telephone, voice mail, paging, electronic mail and internet services.

The latest approvals bring to 111 the number of private companies so far given approval by the NCC to provide telecommunications services alongside the government-owned Nigerian Telecommunications (NITEL).
The licencing of private firms is Nigeria's so-called gradual deregulation of the communications sector. Operators have called for its outright privatisation.

Out of 63 firms licensed between 1995 and April 1996, Telecel Nigeria Ltd had its licence withdrawn over its alleged inability to meet terms stipulated by the NCC. The terms include payment of licencing fees and a readiness to commence operations within six months.
Telecel, the only firm whose licence permitted nationwide coverage, would have been in a position to compete nationally with M.Tel, a subsidiary of NITEL offering mobile telephone services.
